title: Verdier biduality over a finite coefficient field
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ (separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, and finite type means its structure morphism has finite type) [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the derived-complete integral constructible categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. For each finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and let $D_{X,R}=R\mathcal Hom_R(-,\omega_{X,R})$ be integral duality [thm-coef-integral-verdier], with the integral dualizing object of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Then integral duality induces an exact $E$-linear anti-equivalence
$$D_{X,E}:D^b_c(X,E)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_c(X,E).$$
Its evaluation and natural isomorphism $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,E}D_{X,E}K$ are obtained by rationalizing integral evaluation and biduality. The dualizing object is the image $\omega_{X,E}$ of $\omega_{X,R}$. Tensor products and evaluation at the rational stage use the coefficient-passage operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with completed derived tensor at the integral stage. For finite coefficient-field extensions $E\subset L$, the rationalization of the canonical integral comparison [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] is a natural isomorphism
$$(D_{X,E}K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,L}(K\otimes_E L),$$
commuting with evaluation and $\delta$, and satisfying the unit and associator equations for scalar extension.

proof.text: For every finite coefficient field and coherent integral dualizing datum, choose a rational duality datum with natural signed symmetry, together with that naturality proof, supplied by lem-coef-rational-verdier-datum. These choices are local witnesses inside a proposition proof, not definitions of arbitrary data.

For each coefficient embedding and each pair of coherent dualizing data, choose a normalized comparison supplied by lem-coef-rational-verdier-extension (applied with the two naturality proofs), and retain its ExtensionProperties proof.

Apply the identity comparison lemma to the chosen self-extension and the composition comparison lemma to every chosen composable triple. Their normalized unit and associator witnesses are precisely the two remaining conjunctions in Conclusion. Package the two families, their normalization proofs and these witnesses.

proof_origin.place: Assemble the single-field datum, single-extension comparison, unit and associator clauses; existing statement retained.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the structure map, and
$\omega_{X,E}=Ra^!_EE\in D^b_c(X,E)$ the dualizing object of the condensed
category $D^b_c(X,E)$ ([def-sf-setting], [sk-thm-existence]). Put

$$
D_{X,E}K=R\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(K,\omega_{X,E}).
$$

Then $D_{X,E}$ is an exact $E$-linear anti-equivalence

$$
D_{X,E}:D^b_c(X,E)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_c(X,E),
$$

with natural isomorphism $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,E}D_{X,E}K$ given by
evaluation. On integral models it is integral duality with $\ell$ inverted:
$\omega_{X,E}\cong\omega_{X,\mathcal O_E}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, and for
$K_0\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ there is a natural isomorphism
$D_{X,E}(K_0\otimes E)\cong(D_{X,\mathcal O_E}K_0)\otimes E$ carrying
$\delta_{K_0\otimes E}$ to $\delta_{K_0}\otimes E$.
For $E\subset L$, the canonical comparison

$$
(D_{X,E}K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}
D_{X,L}(K\otimes_E L)
$$

commutes with evaluation and $\delta$, and satisfies the unit
and associator equations for scalar extension.

proof.text:
Write $(-)_E=-\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}E_X$; it is exact, since $E_X$ is flat
over $\mathcal O_{E,X}$. By [sk-prop-scalar-six], applied to the coefficient
map $\mathcal O_E\to E$, the coefficient comparisons for the exceptional
inverse image and for internal Hom are isomorphisms on $D^b_c$:

$$
(\omega_{X,\mathcal O_E})_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,E},
\qquad
R\mathcal Hom(K_0,M_0)_E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom((K_0)_E,(M_0)_E)
$$

for $K_0,M_0\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Together they give a natural
isomorphism $\beta_{K_0}:(D_{X,\mathcal O_E}K_0)_E\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,E}((K_0)_E)$.
It is compatible with evaluation, because the internal Hom comparison is the
transpose of scalar-extended evaluation. Transposing once more, it is
compatible with the double-dual maps: $\delta_{(K_0)_E}$ corresponds to
$(\delta_{K_0})_E$. The integral $\delta_{K_0}$ is an isomorphism
([thm-coef-integral-verdier]; its hypotheses hold for all of
$D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]), so
$\delta_{(K_0)_E}$ is an isomorphism.

Every object of $D^b_c(X,E)$ is isomorphic to $(K_0)_E$ for some
$K_0\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ ([sk-lem-integral-models], (4), and
[sk-thm-sfb-rationalization-comparison]). Since $\delta$ is natural, $\delta_K$
is an isomorphism for every $K\in D^b_c(X,E)$. The functor $D_{X,E}$ preserves
$D^b_c(X,E)$, because $D_{X,E}((K_0)_E)\cong(D_{X,\mathcal O_E}K_0)_E$ and
$D_{X,\mathcal O_E}K_0\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$. It is exact and $E$-linear as
an internal Hom into a fixed object. With $D_{X,E}^2\cong\operatorname{id}$ via
$\delta$, it is an anti-equivalence.

For $E\subset L$, extension of scalars along $E_X\to L_X$ is flat
([sk-prop-sfb-finite-extension-compatibility]), and [sk-prop-scalar-six]
gives the comparisons $(\omega_{X,E})_L\cong\omega_{X,L}$ and the internal Hom
comparison. Their composite is the stated comparison. Compatibility with
evaluation and $\delta$ follows by transposition as above. The unit and
associator equations hold because the comparisons of [sk-prop-scalar-six]
respect composition of coefficient maps. On integral models this comparison
is $\beta_{L/E}$ of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] with $\ell$
inverted, by the same compatibility with composition along
$\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_L\to L$ and $\mathcal O_E\to E\to L$.
